title: IS12:: encrypt.c (117.3)

lines.explanation: This demonstrates that a defined constant could be really an expression. This expression is written to count how many lower case letters are in ASCII
This demonstrates that a defined constant could be really an expression. This expression is written to count how many upper case letters are in ASCII
Variable ch will be used to read characters from the standard input. It is defined as int since it should be able to get the EOF value that is not char
When the condition of this while loop is executed, a new character is read from the standard input and assigned to ch. If it is EOF, the loop is over
This comound condition checkes whether ch is a lower case letter
Here we convert the character code into the number among lower case letters. 'a' will be converted to 0, 'b' will be converted to 1 etc.
This comound condition checkes whether ch is an upper case letter
Here we convert the character code into the number among lower case letters. 'A' will be converted to 0, 'A' will be converted to 1 etc.
(charnum + SHIFT) % NLCHARS takes care about cyclic shift of a each number from 1 to 26 and adding it to 'A' converts it back to a valid upper case letter code
If it is not one of the letters, we simply pass the character through.
